concerns.text: T016 introduces a fallback to Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering (HAC) if K-means fails. The spec (FR-002, FR-002a) strictly mandates K-means with adaptive k-reduction. Introducing HAC is a semantic weakening of the specified algorithmic constraint, altering the 'non-neural approximation' methodology without explicit spec authorization.

T022 mandates training BOTH Decision Trees and CGMMs to select the best. FR-003 states the system must train 'a lightweight probabilistic model (Decision Tree or GMM)'. While training both is an enhancement, it doubles the computational cost and complexity, potentially violating SC-003 (CPU-only, 6h runtime) without explicit spec authorization for this comparative scope.

T032c and T033 rely on a 'VLA Proxy Baseline' artifact provided by the user or prior phase. SC-001 and FR-006 require comparison against the 'original Qwen-VLA model' or its proxy. The tasks fail to define how to generate this proxy if it doesn't exist, effectively narrowing the scope from 'original model' to 'user-provided proxy' without a task to generate it, risking an unexecutable FR-006.

T042 tasks measure aggregate pipeline memory usage. SC-003 specifically constrains the 'computational cost... of the non-neural inference' (US-02). Conflating pipeline-wide memory with the specific inference constraint misaligns the verification effort with the defined success criterion.
